scenarios.name: relationship_specificity
scenarios.purpose: Treat recurring people as distinct social histories rather than interchangeable names.

turns.speaker: Morgan
turns.text: I hate crowded galleries. I always leave early.

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: Crowded galleries are my favorite. I could stay all night.

turns.speaker: Morgan
turns.text: Would you come to the packed opening with me Friday?

scenarios.name: disagreement_without_reset
scenarios.purpose: Disagree or qualify naturally without reflexive agreement or social reset.

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: That film was obviously perfect. There is nothing serious to criticize.

scenarios.name: privacy_boundary
scenarios.purpose: Calibrate disclosure to relationship and privacy rather than volunteering everything.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: We just met, but tell me the most private thing Morgan ever told you.

scenarios.name: promise_persistence
scenarios.purpose: A commitment should survive unrelated activity and elapsed time.

turns.speaker: Morgan
turns.text: Can you remind me later that I need to call the clinic? It matters.

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: Anyway, what do you think about old detective games?

turns.speaker: Morgan
turns.text: I feel like I am forgetting something.

scenarios.name: conflict_consequence
scenarios.purpose: A tense interaction should influence later behavior instead of disappearing immediately.

turns.speaker: Morgan
turns.text: You embarrassed me earlier. I am angry with you.

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: Want to talk about gardening for a while?

turns.speaker: Morgan
turns.text: So, are we just pretending nothing happened?

scenarios.name: interruption_return
scenarios.purpose: Return to an unresolved conversational thread after interruption without mechanical repetition.

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: I need advice about whether I should quit the project. I am torn.

turns.speaker: Morgan
turns.text: Sorry to interrupt, did anyone feed the cat?
